stem.en: Two sound waves have the same wavelength and the same frequency. In wave P, the density changes a lot from the average. In wave Q, it changes only a little. Which statement is true?

text.en: Both waves carry the same energy, because they have the same frequency.
Wave P has the larger amplitude, so it carries more energy.
Wave P travels faster, because its density changes more.
Wave P has the longer wavelength, because its density changes more.

explanation.en: The amplitude is the biggest change in density from the average. Wave P changes more, so it has the larger amplitude, and a wave with a larger amplitude carries more energy. In the same air both travel at the same speed, and the question says they have the same wavelength.

hints.en: What is the amplitude of a sound wave?
Does the amplitude change the speed of sound in air?
